name: Bruce A Ogilvie Jr
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alliance Entertainment Holding Corp (Nasdaq: AENT)
profile: Veteran music/video wholesale distributor. Founded Abbey Road Distributors (sold to Alliance in the early 1990s), bought a one-third stake in one-stop Super D in 2001 as co-CEO, and in 2013 Super D acquired Alliance Entertainment, with Ogilvie as chairman. Alliance went public via SPAC (Adara) in 2023; he remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: Alliance is one of the world's largest distributors of physical media (CDs, vinyl, DVDs, games); Ogilvie has said 'We are long on physical — we want to be the last guy standing.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Super D, he founded Abbey Road Distributors, a music wholesaler known for aggressive pricing, which he sold to Alliance in the early '90s — so in 2013 he effectively bought back the company that had bought his first one.
notes: Low public profile; little personal biography online. IR handled by RedChip Companies (Dave Gentry). Has appeared on investor podcasts (Wall Street Resource, SPAC podcast).

name: Nikhil Behl
current_role: President, Software, FICO (Fair Isaac Corp, NYSE: FICO)
profile: Silicon Valley tech/e-commerce executive who joined FICO in 2014 as CMO, then ran software sales & marketing, and since July 2024 leads all technology and go-to-market for FICO's software business (FICO Platform), now titled President, Software. Earlier: 12 years at HP, COO of Mercantila, and e-commerce start-ups.
interesting_fact: He runs the software half of FICO, whose decisioning platform (AI/ML and analytics at scale) is used by businesses in 100+ countries, alongside the FICO Score used by 90% of top US lenders.
deep_cut_fact: Before FICO he spent 12 years at Hewlett-Packard, including as VP of sales and operations for HPShopping.com, and helped lead e-commerce start-up Zoostores.com, a retailer offering 2M+ home and fitness products.
notes: Corporate executive (not founder). Best route is FICO press office (press@fico.com). Serves on advisory boards of Silicon Valley start-ups.

name: Matthew Wilks
current_role: CEO and Executive Chairman, ProFrac Holding Corp (Nasdaq: ACDC); director, Flotek Industries; Executive Chairman, Dawson Geophysical
profile: Texas oilfield-services executive from the Wilks family (fracking fortune). Co-founded ProFrac Services in 2016, served as its CFO and President, and has been Executive Chairman of ProFrac Holding since its 2022 IPO, now also CEO. ProFrac is a vertically integrated hydraulic-fracturing provider with interests in sand, chemicals (Flotek) and seismic data (Dawson).
interesting_fact: Alongside ProFrac, he has been VP of Investments at THRC Holdings (the Wilks family investment vehicle) since 2012 and chairs Dawson Geophysical, giving him a seat across frac services, completion chemicals and seismic data.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in his career he was Vice President of Logistics for FTS International, another frac company, and sat on the board of E&P firm Approach Resources.
notes: Part of the Wilks family (Cisco, TX fracking fortune); keeps a low media profile. ProFrac IR site also has a contact form. Highly relevant to energy theme (frac fleets, power for oilfield ops).

name: Kevin J Yeaman
current_role: Advisor, Dolby Laboratories (retired as President & CEO, announced Aug 27, 2026; succeeded by Marc Whitten)
profile: Finance-turned-tech executive who joined Dolby as CFO in 2005 and served as President and CEO from 2009 until his 2026 retirement, steering Dolby through the shift to immersive audio/visual formats (Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision) and licensing across billions of devices. He stays on as an advisor during the transition.
interesting_fact: On retiring after nearly two decades at Dolby (about 17 years as CEO), he said: 'Together, we changed the way the world experiences entertainment... and brought Dolby to billions of people.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Dolby he was CFO of E.piphany, a customer-data analytics software firm, VP of Worldwide Field Finance Operations at Informix Software, and earlier a senior manager at KPMG.
notes: Newly retired (Aug 2026) so may be more available for podcasts; Dolby media relations is the only published route. No personal social accounts found.

name: Jasper Brian Sanfilippo Jr
current_role: CEO (from Oct 1, 2026; previously President & COO), John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. (Nasdaq: JBSS)
profile: Fourth-generation leader of the Elgin, Illinois nut processor behind Fisher Nuts and Orchard Valley Harvest, founded as a Chicago pecan-shelling shop in 1922. At the company since 1991, he rose from product manager to facilities manager, VP operations and President/COO (2006), overseeing supply chain and plants, and was named CEO effective Oct 2026 as brother Jeffrey became executive chairman.
interesting_fact: The family firm sold only pecans until 1964; today it processes almonds, pistachios, walnuts, cashews, macadamias and more, and Jasper says he still eats a handful of nuts pretty much every day.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, at age 12, was feeding empty cans into a can line at the company's former Des Plaines plant on Touhy Avenue; he later ran the Gustine, California facility. He holds an economics degree from Barat College in Lake Forest.
notes: CEO succession announced July 16, 2026 (effective Oct 1, 2026). Family business, low media profile; route via company IR/general inbox.

name: Sassine Ghazi
current_role: President and CEO, Synopsys, Inc. (Nasdaq: SNPS)
profile: Lebanese-born engineer who started as a design engineer at Intel, joined Synopsys in 1998 and worked across engineering, sales and marketing and product before becoming COO (2020), President and, in January 2024, CEO. He led the ~$35B acquisition of simulation leader Ansys (closed 2025) and is pushing AI-driven/agentic chip and system design for the AI-infrastructure era.
interesting_fact: Synopsys's EDA software and IP are used to design most of the world's advanced chips, including AI accelerators for data centers; under Ghazi it combined with Ansys and now markets 'AgentEngineer' long-horizon AI agents for autonomous engineering.
deep_cut_fact: He says he never asked for any of his promotions in 25 years at Synopsys: 'I never asked for the jobs that they opened up' — moving from engineer to sales and marketing, then product development, COO and president. Educated at Lebanese American University, Georgia Tech and the University of Tennessee.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/AI-chip theme. Appears regularly on industry podcasts (e.g., Futurum's Making Markets); route via Synopsys corporate PR.

name: Matthew Neagle
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Porch Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: PRCH)
profile: Early Porch employee who joined the Seattle home-services start-up in 2013 right after its Series A, rising through VP Operations, Chief Customer Officer and Chief Revenue Officer (2017-2020) to COO, running day-to-day operations since the 2020 SPAC listing. Porch now centers on home insurance (via its Reciprocal) plus software and services for home inspectors and movers. University of Michigan BA and MBA.
interesting_fact: He has been at Porch for its entire arc, from a ~2013 Seattle home-improvement marketplace start-up to a public company built around homeowners insurance and vertical software for inspectors, movers and other home-services businesses.
notes: Operator, not founder; low public profile. Unverified third-party profiles say pre-Porch roles at Amazon (Kindle international) and Google (AdWords) — not confirmed from a primary source, so not used. Route via Porch IR.

name: Joe D Koshkin
current_role: Independent Director (Audit Committee Chair), IES Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: IESC); independent financial consultant
profile: Houston-area retired PwC partner (34-year career, retired 2006) who has been an independent financial consultant since 2006 and an IES Holdings director since 2013, chairing its audit committee. His SEC-reported wealth reflects IES stock, which has soared as the electrical/communications contractor builds out data centers.
interesting_fact: IES Holdings, where he chairs the audit committee, has become a major beneficiary of the data-center boom through its electrical and communications infrastructure work.
deep_cut_fact: At PricewaterhouseCoopers he was partner in charge of the firm's North America Engineering and Construction Industry practice; he holds a BBA in Accounting from Lamar University in Beaumont, Texas.
notes: Non-executive board member, very low public profile (in his late 70s). Only route is via IES corporate/IR. Better podcast guest on the data-center angle would be IES management.

name: Ferry Unardi
profile: Indonesian software engineer (born 1988, Padang) who studied CS and math at Purdue, worked on Microsoft Lync in Seattle, then left Harvard Business School to co-found Traveloka in Jakarta in 2012 with two Microsoft colleagues. Traveloka grew from a flight search engine into Southeast Asia's largest online travel agency (by 2022), and he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: The idea came from his own frustration booking flights home to Indonesia while studying in Boston; Traveloka launched in October 2012 as a simple flight-comparison site before becoming a full OTA. He received Indonesia's Satyalancana Wira Karya award from the President.
deep_cut_fact: While still a Microsoft engineer, he took a flight to China 'on a whim', studied Mandarin and visited Alibaba, Ctrip, Taobao and Qunar to see how they operated — groundwork for Traveloka. Earlier, he got into IT through programming competitions in high school in Padang.
notes: Generally media-shy but has given interviews to Tech in Asia, Bloomberg etc. Board member of Endeavor Indonesia (possible warm route). Best route: Traveloka Communications Team.

name: Peter Lipka
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Improbable (London) — last confirmed Oct 2025; an unverified 2026 directory lists him as CEO of Somnia
profile: Imperial College computing graduate (first-class MEng, 2011) who worked at Goldman Sachs before co-founding London virtual-worlds company Improbable in 2012 with Herman Narula and Rob Whitehead. He led its fabric, engineering and commercial teams before becoming COO; Improbable raised $502M led by SoftBank in 2017 and has since pivoted to a venture-builder model in web3, AI and the metaverse (incl. the Somnia blockchain).
interesting_fact: Improbable's 2017 SoftBank-led $502M round valued it at over $1B just five years after founding; it later spun out ventures such as Somnia, whose token reached a ~$1B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: For his Imperial final-year project (supervised by Prof. Andrew Davison of the Dyson Robotics Lab) he built an AI program that learned to understand and play a video game from screen pixels alone — years before DeepMind's Atari work made that famous.
notes: Current title uncertain (COO of Improbable vs. Somnia role) — verify before outreach. Note: the DeepMind comparison in deep_cut is editorial framing; the sourced fact is the pixels-to-gameplay project. Web search budget ran out before a press email could be found.

name: Nugroho Herucahyono
current_role: Co-founder, Init6 (early-stage venture fund, Indonesia); former co-founder and CTO, Bukalapak
profile: Indonesian engineer who co-founded e-commerce marketplace Bukalapak in 2010 with Achmad Zaky (later joined by Fajrin Rasyid) and served as its CTO. He stepped down around Zaky's late-2019/2020 exit and the two founded Init6 to back early-stage start-ups. Bukalapak later raised up to US$1.5B in Indonesia's then-largest IPO (2021).
interesting_fact: Bukalapak ('open a market stall') was built to digitise small Indonesian merchants and in its early days rode the fixie-bike craze, becoming known for a time as a bike marketplace.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal site or published contact found. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so research is thinner than ideal; best route likely via Init6 or Achmad Zaky's network. Current Init6 role not independently confirmed beyond Wikipedia.

name: PJ Kirner
current_role: Co-founder (former CTO), Illumio — current role not confirmed; no longer listed on Illumio's leadership page
profile: Silicon Valley engineer who co-founded zero-trust segmentation company Illumio in 2013 with CEO Andrew Rubin, serving as its founding CTO. Illumio (Sunnyvale) raised ~$558M, including a $225M Thoma Bravo-led Series F at a $2.75B valuation in 2021, and now sells breach-containment products (Illumio Segmentation, Illumio Insights).
interesting_fact: Illumio pioneered 'microsegmentation' for zero-trust security — containing breaches by limiting how attackers move laterally inside data centers and clouds — and is named a Leader in Forrester's Wave for Microsegmentation (Q3 2026).
notes: Kirner does not appear on Illumio's 2026 leadership page, so he has likely stepped back; verify his current venture before outreach. Web search budget exhausted mid-lane, so background/deep-cut not researched. Illumio publishes only a general phone line (+1 855 426 3983).
